title: Hold a mango cheek steady, score it into a grid down to but not through the skin, then push the skin up to fan the cubes
instruction: Steady the mango cheek, score its flesh into a crosshatch grid down to the skin with the paring knife without cutting through the skin, press the skin side onto the upturned ramekin so the cubes fan out, then leave the cheek and the knife on the board and let go.
context: The usual way to cube a mango: cut a cheek off beside the seed, then (mango.org) "Score (slice) the flesh in a crosshatch pattern, without cutting through the skin" and push the skin's centre up so the cubes fan out. The skin under the flat cut face is a cup, 24 mm deep in the middle and nothing at the edge, so the knife point must follow it down and up on every cut: too shallow and the cubes stay joined, too deep and the skin is cut.
setup: Station bench, top z=0.7475 m; x away from the robot, y to its left. OXO Good Grips 11272900 polypropylene cutting board, 535.9 x 368.3 mm, 16 mm thick (estimated), fixed, centre (0.29, 0), long side along y, top z=0.7635. One cheek of a ripe Ataulfo (Honey) mango, cut off beside the seed by the assessor at reset, lying skin side down: flat cut face 112 x 72 mm, 25.5 mm deep at the middle (24 mm flesh on 1.5 mm skin), outer skin half an ellipsoid, 115 g (estimates; acceptance bands in README). Mercer Millennia M23900P paring knife (76 mm blade, 100 x 22 x 24 mm handle, 50 g; handle and mass estimated) standing on the flat underside of its handle, blade pointing -y. Upturned white porcelain 2 fl oz ramekin (60 mm rim, 48 mm base, 32 mm tall, 100 g, estimated), loose. Steel ruler 300 x 20 x 2 mm beyond the board at (0.49, 0). Lot A (screenshot): cheek cut-face centre (0.310, -0.090), long axis 45 degrees right of straight ahead, narrow end toward the left arm; knife handle centre (0.240, -0.135); ramekin (0.410, -0.210). Lot B: cheek (0.300, -0.072), long axis 33 degrees right of ahead; knife (0.215, -0.140); ramekin (0.400, -0.200). No jitter; the simulation checks each start within 4 mm and 3 degrees.
scoring: Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: the knife edge goes more than 1 mm into the 1.5 mm skin more than 2 mm in from the cheek's edge (cut through); the blade touches a gripper or comes within 10 mm of a gripper not holding the knife by its handle; the skin is pushed in more than 35 mm, past a full inside-out turn, while a gripper holds the cheek (split). Otherwise judged at the end, with both grippers at least 5 mm from cheek, knife and ramekin, the cheek skin side down on the board, knife and ramekin resting on the board, no blade within 2 mm of the cheek, and nothing moving over 1 mm or 2 degrees for 1 s; if not, 0. A cube is a piece of the cut face separated from every other by cuts reaching within 6 mm of the skin (flesh within 7 mm of the edge is rim), 80-800 mm2 on top, no two points over 30 mm apart. 1.0: at least 10 cubes, and after they were cut the skin's middle was pushed up at least 12 mm (from below the cut face) onto the base-up ramekin while a gripper pinched the cheek. 0.75: at least 10 cubes, not pushed. 0.5: 5-9 cubes. 0.25: one connected run of cut flesh (within 6 mm of the skin, outside the 7 mm rim) whose bounding box is 30 mm or more corner to corner. 0: otherwise. A cut counts only with the knife held by its handle, the cheek pinched by the other hand (opening 10-90 mm, both fingertips within 3 mm of the cheek, contacts 15 mm or more apart), the blade within 45 degrees of upright, the edge moving at 1 mm/s or more within 45 degrees of its own plane, against the stated drag. Real trial: a cut counts wherever it parts the flesh to within 6 mm of the skin; top photo with the ruler to count and measure cubes, the knife tip and a depth gauge to check each cut reaches within 6 mm of the skin, the skin held to a light for slits (the simulation's 1 mm-into-the-skin rule is a stricter stand-in), a side video with a 1 mm scale for the push, side and top videos for the 10 mm blade gap, video for the end conditions. Lots A and B averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: Real trial: a new Ataulfo (Honey) mango (280-350 g; a 10 N press with a 20 mm flat probe dents it 2-4 mm; no bruises) per trial. The assessor stands it on its stem end and cuts one cheek off about 6 mm beside the centre line, clearing the seed; keep it if the cut face is 105-120 mm long and 66-78 mm wide and 23-28 mm deep at the middle, else cut the other side or a new fruit. Weigh and photograph it with the ruler. Board, knife and ramekin washed and dried; new cut-resistant pad covers. Simulation: each trial writes the lot's exact start poses and resets the cut record.
fidelity: True size. The cheek is one rigid 115 g half-ellipsoid of boxes; the blade has no collider. Declared cut: a 1 mm cell of the face is cut where the held, upright edge passes within 6 mm of the 1.5 mm skin, with the cheek pinched, against up to 1 N drag and 1 N feed resistance (estimates, rising with speed). Over 1 mm into the skin cuts it. The ramekin passes into the rigid cheek: 12-25.5 mm (base centre below the face) is pushed up; over 35 mm while held is a split. Cuts show as dark 4 mm marks.
scores: demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0); Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0, step limit). Earlier Dream-1 runs on earlier versions of the task: two complete runs, 0.0 in both lots each; two launches stopped unscored when the task changed
